Build the IPCC 2019 wet/dry moisture regime of WHEP's crop land.

Source: R/moisture_regime.R
build_cell_moisture_regime.Rd

Classify each cell, polity, commodity balance item, water regime and year of WHEP's own crop land use as IPCC 2019 wet or dry, the classes the Tier 1 managed-soil factors are keyed on.

A zone is tropical where the mean annual temperature exceeds 18 degC and there are at most 7 frost days per year (IPCC 2019 Refinement, Volume 4, Chapter 3, Figure 3A.5.2, p. 3.48). A tropical row is wet where its annual water exceeds 1000 mm; any other row is wet where its annual water divided by potential evapotranspiration (PET) exceeds 1; every other row is dry. Both tests are strict, so a value of exactly 1 or exactly 1000 mm is dry (Volume 4, Chapter 11, Table 11.1, footnote 4, p. 11.13). Footnote 4 bases the disaggregation on long-term averages, so by default the inputs are averaged over the 30 years ending in each year before they are classified.

The water term is precipitation plus, on irrigated rows, the irrigation depth of the row's crops (water = "precip_irrig", the default), or precipitation alone (water = "precip"). Rainfed rows get no irrigation.

Usage

build_cell_moisture_regime(
  years = NULL,
  window = c("trailing_30", "annual", "normal"),
  water = c("precip_irrig", "precip"),
  data = NULL,
  config = list(),
  example = FALSE
)

Source

IPCC (2019), 2019 Refinement to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Volume 4: Chapter 3, Figure 3A.5.2 (p. 3.48); Chapter 11, Table 11.1, footnote 4 (p. 11.13).

CRU TS version 4.09 (files cru_ts4.09.1901.2024.<var>.dat.nc), Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia.

Arguments

years

Integer vector of the years to classify.

window

How the inputs are averaged before they are classified: "trailing_30" (default, the 30 years ending in each year), "annual" or "normal" (one fixed period, config$normal_period).

water

The water term: "precip_irrig" (default, precipitation plus the irrigation depth of the row's crops and regime) or "precip".

data

Optional list of inputs used in place of reading them. Each element is optional:

  • climate: lon, lat, year, mean_annual_temp_c, annual_precip_mm, annual_pet_mm, annual_frost_days; its years are the climate record.

  • crop_depth: the LPJmL irrigation depth per cell, crop and year (lon, lat, year, lpjml_crop, irrig_mm_irrigated, irrig_mm_rainfed, stand_frac_irrigated, stand_frac_rainfed, lpjml_version, lpjml_git_hash, lpjml_run).

  • lpjml_years: the years the LPJmL run covers (default: the years of crop_depth).

  • lpjml_grid: the cells (lon, lat) the LPJmL run's output covers. Needed with crop_depth when an irrigated row's crop has no irrigated LPJmL stand in its cell; otherwise read from the run.

  • regime_areas: WHEP's rainfed and irrigated hectares (lon, lat, area_code, item_prod_code, year, rainfed_ha, irrigated_ha).

  • country_grid: the cell support the regime areas are built on when they are not supplied.

config

Optional list: cru_dir (default WHEP_CRU_DIR), run_dir (default WHEP_LPJML_RUN_DIR, else the pinned depth layer), normal_period (default 1991:2020) and max_rows (default 2e6, the classifier input rows per block of cells, about 1.3 KB each at peak).

example

If TRUE, return a small fixture instead of reading data. Defaults to FALSE.

Value

A tibble with one row per lon, lat, area_code, item_cbs_code, water_regime and year where WHEP has hectares of that regime, carrying the window-mean mat_c, frost_days, prec_mm, pet_mm and irrig_mm, water_mm, moisture_ratio, tropical, moisture_regime ("wet", "dry" or NA), method_moisture_regime, climate_fill_km (the distance to the CRU cell whose climate variables a cell lacking some took, NA for a cell with all of its own), method_irrig_depth, lpjml_crop and the LPJmL vintage columns lpjml_version, lpjml_git_hash and lpjml_run, plus the polity columns below.

An irrigated row's irrigation is averaged over the window years in which WHEP irrigates that land, its climate over the whole window; a row irrigated in fewer than all of them carries irrig_years_<n>of<m> in method_moisture_regime. Where WHEP irrigates a crop the LPJmL run has no irrigated stand of in the cell, in a year the run covers, the depth is the crop's LPJmL depth averaged over the polity's cells that have the stand, weighted by WHEP's irrigated hectares, and method_irrig_depth says why: lpjml_landuse_vintage for a cell on the LPJmL grid (the run's land-use forcing differs from WHEP's there) or no_lpjml_cell for one outside it, with the suffix _world_mean where the polity has no such stand and the world's mean is used. A message of class whep_moisture_regime_stand_gap counts these rows and hectares by cause; its diagnosis field lists every case.

Details

Inputs:

  • Climate comes from CRU TS: annual mean temperature, precipitation, PET and ground-frost days. CRU ships PET as a mean daily rate in mm per day, which is multiplied by the days of each month and summed over the year. CRU's frost count is synthetic: CRU derives it from the gridded minimum temperature. Years before the CRU record (1901) hold the 1901-1930 climatology, and years after it hold the climatology of its last 30 years. A cell of WHEP's crop land that holds no value of a CRU variable in any year (all four for a cell off CRU's land mask, mostly coastal and island cells; fewer for a cell CRU maps for some variables only) takes that variable's whole record from its nearest CRU land cell by great-circle distance between cell centres, among the cells that hold it in every year read. One donor supplies every variable the cell lacks, and the cell keeps the variables it has; a variable with gaps is not lent but left to the classifier, which reports the years without it. The distance is climate_fill_km, and a message of class whep_moisture_regime_nearest_climate counts the cells by the variables they took. The cell's own water term, irrigation included, is then applied.

  • Irrigation depth is LPJmL's applied irrigation per crop stand, pooled to the commodity balance item by WHEP's irrigated hectares. LPJmL's paddy water on its rainfed rice stand is not counted: rainfed rows get none.

Irrigation depth stamps

method_irrig_depth holds the least direct method over the window years of the row's irrigation record, one of:

  • lpjml_airrig_stand: the item's own LPJmL crop has an irrigated stand in the cell.

  • lpjml_crop_proxy: another named LPJmL crop stands in for the item, as mapped in regime_yield_crop_mapping (fodder crops, for example).

  • lpjml_others_proxy: the item sits on LPJmL's composite "others" stand of minor crops.

  • lpjml_landuse_vintage: WHEP irrigates the crop in a cell of the LPJmL grid where the run has no irrigated stand of it, because the run's land-use forcing predates WHEP's current land use. The depth is the crop's mean over the polity's cells that have the stand, weighted by WHEP's irrigated hectares.

  • no_lpjml_cell: the same fill for a cell outside the LPJmL grid.

  • lpjml_landuse_vintage_world_mean and no_lpjml_cell_world_mean: the two fills above where the polity has no such stand that year, so the world's mean over the cells that have it is used.

  • rainfed_regime: a rainfed row, zero by definition.

  • NA: water = "precip", where there is no irrigation term.

A stamp carries two optional additions. The suffix _recycled_climate follows any of the seven LPJmL-derived methods above when a window year precedes 1901, because LPJmL recycles the 1901-1930 weather before its forcing starts. The field ;outside_run_<n>of<m>_<fill> follows it when n of the window's m years lie outside the LPJmL run: those years take the mean of the series' own window years inside the run (<fill> is series_mean) or, where it has none, its country's mean for the balance item (country_mean).

Moisture regime stamps

method_moisture_regime joins these fields with ;, in this order:

  • ipcc2019_wet_dry: the rule.

  • The window: annual, trailing_30 or normal_<first>_<last>.

  • The water term: precip or precip_irrig.

  • Optional climatology_<first>_<last>_<n>of<m>: n of the window's m years lie outside the CRU record and took the held climatology of the years <first> to <last>.

  • Optional irrig_years_<n>of<m>: an irrigated row whose land is irrigated in n of the window's m years. Its irrigation is the mean of those n years and its climate the mean of all m.

  • Optional nearest_cru_cell=<col>[+<col>...]: the cell lacks these CRU climate variables (mat_c, frost_days, prec_mm, pet_mm) and took them from its nearest CRU land cell, climate_fill_km away; its other variables are its own.

  • Optional, on an unclassified row (moisture_regime is NA): missing=<col>[+<col>...], the inputs whose window mean is unavailable, and pet_not_positive, a window-mean PET of zero. Nothing is zero-filled.

Errors

The function aborts, with these condition classes, when:

  • whep_moisture_regime_years: years is NULL, empty or has a missing value.

  • whep_moisture_regime_config: config has an unknown entry, or max_rows is not one positive number.

  • whep_moisture_regime_period: normal_period is not a run of consecutive whole years.

  • whep_moisture_regime_columns, whep_moisture_regime_empty, whep_moisture_regime_key, whep_moisture_regime_climate: an input table lacks a required column, has no rows, has a duplicated or missing key, or carries more than one climate for a cell-year; or no cell of the climate holds, in every year read, a variable that a cell lacks.

  • whep_moisture_regime_domain: an input holds a negative precipitation, PET, frost count or irrigation depth, more than 366 frost days, a water_regime other than "rainfed" or "irrigated", or irrigation on a rainfed row.

  • whep_moisture_regime_lpjml_grid: data$crop_depth has stand gaps but no data$lpjml_grid is supplied.

  • whep_moisture_regime_stand_mapping: an irrigated production item has no LPJmL crop band.

  • whep_moisture_regime_stand_no_mean: a crop has no irrigated LPJmL stand anywhere that year, so there is no depth to fill from.

  • whep_moisture_regime_outside_run: an irrigated series-year outside the LPJmL run has no depth of its own or of its country to fill from.

  • whep_absent_input: precipitation, PET, the irrigated hectares or the irrigation depth of the irrigated rows is absent, missing or all zero.

  • whep_lpjml_irrig_depth_*: the LPJmL irrigation depth layer rejects the regime areas, the run or its output cubes, or the pinned layer.

Messages of class whep_moisture_regime_unclassified, whep_moisture_regime_area_years and whep_moisture_regime_nearest_climate report rows left without a regime, window years the regime areas do not cover and cells that took climate variables from their nearest CRU cell.

Polity columns

Every area-keyed output carries the polity its area_code resolves to in that row's year:

  • polity_area_code: The numeric key rows are AGGREGATED on, for the matrix workflows. It is a bucket, not an identity: use reporting_polity_code to say which territory a row belongs to.

  • reporting_polity_code: The polity itself, e.g. ESP-1846-1914. It is year-aware, so the same area_code resolves to different polities in different years, which is the point of the crosswalk.

  • reporting_polity_name: Its name. It can differ from the area's own name where the area folds into an aggregate.

  • reporting_polity_has_geometry: Whether the polity has a polygon in the WHEP polity database, for callers that need to map or intersect it. FALSE is a documented gap upstream, not an error.

Rows whose area_code resolves to no polity keep the columns with NA rather than being dropped, so a gap is visible instead of silent.

Rows before the back-cast anchor year resolve to the polity live in that anchor year rather than to the polity live in the row's own year, because WHEP's pre-anchor series are back-cast onto the anchor-year territory. See add_polity_code() for the reasoning. Where that polity is not live in the row's own year – 41.5% of the pre-1961 (area, year) cells – add_polity_code() says so as mapping_status == "backcast_anchor", and polity_coverage_gaps() reports it as gap_kind == "backcast_anchor". These columns do not say so either way.

A row whose year no mapped period covers is resolved to the NEAREST period of the same area instead, so reporting_polity_code can name a polity that did not exist in that row's year – FAOSTAT bucket 206 "Sudan (former)" keeps reporting after SUD-1956-2011 ends, and its post-2011 rows carry that code. These columns do not say so: add_polity_code() reports such a row as mapping_status == "out_of_span", and that column is dropped here so that adding it does not change the schema of every area-keyed output at once. polity_coverage_gaps() reports the stand-in rows of a built table, and options(whep.polity_mapping_status = "flag") (or "status") carries the signal on the outputs themselves. Both are opt-in; the default is no extra column.

Examples

build_cell_moisture_regime(example = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 10 × 26
#>     year area_code polity_area_code reporting_polity_code reporting_polity_name

#>  2  2009        79               79 DEU-1990-2025         Germany

#>  4  2009        79               79 DEU-1990-2025         Germany
